title: Fake login windows in practice
intro: Looks real, but trapped inside the page. Decide what you would do in each moment from this module's lessons.

decisions.title: IshPocht: sign in
decisions.prompt: The window shows the right address. But that proves nothing yet. What do you do?

artifact.title: IshPocht: sign in
body: Sign in with your work email to view the document.

options.label: Drag the window outside the browser
Type the password and sign in

decisions.explain: The right test. Let us see whether the window can leave the browser.

decisions.title: Narmin Hasanova shared a file with you
decisions.prompt: What do you do with this e-mail?

artifact.subject: Narmin Hasanova shared a file with you
body: Note: the budget table we discussed this morning.

decisions.explain: You expected this file, and the link goes to the service's own address. It is fine to open.

decisions.title: IshPocht: sign in
decisions.prompt: The window was cut off at the page edge. A real window never does that. What do you do?

artifact.title: IshPocht: sign in
body: The window reached the edge of the page and was cut off.
It did not leave the browser.

options.label: Close the window and the tab

decisions.explain: A window that cannot leave the page is fake, so type nothing into it.

decisions.title: IshPocht: sign in

artifact.title: IshPocht: sign in
body: You dragged the window aside: it left the browser and moved onto the desktop.
ParolSeyf offered the password by itself.

decisions.explain: The window moves apart from the browser, and the password manager recognises the site. These are signs of a real window.

decisions.title: IshPocht: sign in

artifact.title: IshPocht: sign in
body: It reached the edge of the page and was cut off.

decisions.explain: A real window leaves the browser and goes anywhere on the screen. If it gets cut off, it is a picture drawn inside the page.
